ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, on a smooth horizontal surface, a long wooden block with mass $M$ moves to the right at a constant initial velocity. A small iron block with mass $m$ is gently placed on the right end of the long wooden block without any initial velocity. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the small iron block and the long wooden block is $\mu$. When the small iron block slides a distance $L$ relative to the long wooden block and comes to rest relative to it, the displacement of the long wooden block relative to the ground is $l$. Determine the following during this process:

1. Heat generated by the system
2. The increase in kinetic energy of the small iron block
3. The kinetic energy lost by the long wooden block
4. The reduction in the system's mechanical energy
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
$\mu mg L$
$\mu mg (l - L)$
$\mu mg l$
$\mu mg L$

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: On a smooth horizontal surface, a long wooden block with mass $M$ moves to the right with an initial constant velocity. A small iron block with mass $m$ is gently placed on the right end of the long wooden block with no initial velocity. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the small iron block and the long wooden block is $\mu$. When the small iron block slides a distance $L$ relative to the long wooden block and comes to rest relative to it, the displacement of the long wooden block relative to the ground is $l$. Determine during this process: 1. the heat generated by the system; 2. the increase in kinetic energy of the small iron block; 3. the kinetic energy lost by the long wooden block; 4. the reduction in the system's mechanical energy.
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: $\mu mg L$ $\mu mg (l - L)$ $\mu mg l$ $\mu mg L$
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a long wooden block labeled M, placed on a horizontal surface; a small iron block labeled m is located on the upper surface near the right end of the long wooden block; on the right side there is a velocity arrow v pointing to the right, indicating that the long wooden block moves to the right. No other horizontal external force is shown in the figure, so the horizontal interaction during the sliding stage is taken as the kinetic friction force between the two blocks. Reasoning: The magnitude of the kinetic friction force between the small iron block and the long wooden block is f = μmg. It is known that the displacement of the long wooden block relative to the ground is l, and the distance by which the small iron block slides backward relative to the long wooden block is L, so the displacement of the small iron block relative to the ground is l - L. The heat generated by friction equals the friction force multiplied by the relative sliding distance: Q = fL = μmgL. The friction force on the small iron block is directed to the right, in the same direction as the displacement of the small iron block, so the work done on the small iron block is W_m = f(l - L) = μmg(l - L), which is the increase in the kinetic energy of the small iron block. The friction force on the long wooden block is directed to the left, opposite to the displacement of the long wooden block, so the work done on the long wooden block is W_M = -fl = -μmgl, so the kinetic energy lost by the long wooden block is μmgl. The decrease in the mechanical energy of the system equals the kinetic energy lost by the long wooden block minus the kinetic energy gained by the small iron block, and also equals the heat generated by friction: μmgl - μmg(l - L) = μmgL.
